details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 330-351 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: When a release run has no provider-outage evidence but an outage marker is open, the intake records the run on the marker and exits without diagnosing the unrelated failure.
  WHY: This can leave a real release defect undiagnosed; severity ranges from MAJOR to BLOCKER, and z-ai_glm-5_2 describes the behavior as a documented design trade-off.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 564-581 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: probe_provider() treats any HTTP 200 response as recovery without checking whether the response body reports a provider error.
  WHY: An application-level error in a 200 response can close the outage marker and resume reviews while real model calls still fail.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 830-837 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: _resume() sets recovered=True before the marker-close PATCH loop succeeds.
  WHY: A failed PATCH can return recovered=True with marker_closed=False, misleading operators reading the tick log.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 600-604 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: record() swallows every GitHubError from label creation, rather than only the expected already-exists error.
  WHY: If label creation fails for another reason, the issue may be created without the label or issue creation may fail with a misleading error; severity ranges from NIT to MAJOR.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 305-328 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: latest_review_outcome() accepts an editor-summary comment as the latest outcome without verifying that it belongs to the current head_sha.
  WHY: A stale summary can override the current head’s provider_unavailable failure marker and prevent recovery cleanup.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 595-620 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: record() can create duplicate open outage markers when concurrent callers both observe no marker before either creates one.
  WHY: Duplicate markers and alerts can result, and the attempted duplicate close can fail.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 595-620; .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml lines 92-94, 111-167 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A queued probe tick can resume an outage after an earlier tick has already begun recovery, repeating recovery actions including release-run reruns.
  WHY: Concurrent or queued resume work can duplicate alerts, comments, close attempts, or release reruns.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 826-827 and 835-836 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: _resume() posts its resume comment before the marker PATCH succeeds.
  WHY: A failed close can leave a durable comment that causes a retry to treat work as handled even when a release rerun did not happen.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 819-820 and 838 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When the final resume attempt has errors, the recovery alert can report recovery while the marker is closed and the specific failed work is not made clear in the alert.
  WHY: An operator may miss which consumer repo or release rerun failed unless they follow the marker link.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:line 1549 of count_identical_failures; line 1459 of render_failure_marker; .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:line 168 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The provider_unavailable marker reason is defined in multiple locations, so a future change or typo in one definition can break the shared marker contract.
  WHY: The heal output and check-in parser may then disagree on the reason, disabling the intended cap or streak skip.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:lines 111-167 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The provider-outage probe defaults ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS to true when the operator sets the variable to false.
  WHY: Recovery-triggered review dispatches can therefore run with workflow edits enabled despite the operator’s opt-out.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "a failed release run is recorded on it instead of being diagnosed" (PR DESCRIPTION, agents.md review-autofix section). Issue #5773, per the Copilot review comment (entry[24] of the PR discussion), scopes this to "release runs that failed solely because of `provider_unavailable`"; an unrelated release defect during an outage must continue through the normal intake diagnosis path.
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh, the release-run block at lines 330-351 (specifically the `else` branch at line 342 that calls `provider_outage_record --only-if-open`).
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The current `else` branch unconditionally records the run on the open marker whenever the run's logs have no positive provider-outage evidence; `test_intake_defers_any_release_failure_while_a_marker_is_open_and_diagnoses_otherwise` (in tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py) exercises and expects the marker-open deferral.
- requirement: "It counts toward neither the identical-failure cap nor the heal streak." The implementation must skip the count when a comment is a `provider_unavailable` failure marker.
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py — count_identical_failures() at lines 1524-1560 and count_autofix_failure_streak() at lines 541-558.
  confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The contract tests `test_outage_markers_never_count_toward_the_identical_failure_cap` and `test_outage_comments_never_count_toward_the_heal_streak` exist and pass, but the interaction with `--provider-log-dir` and the new `provider-outage-detect` subcommand is not tested end-to-end.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 341-348 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When an open provider-outage marker exists but a failed release run has no provider evidence in its logs, the intake records the run on the marker without diagnosing it.
  WHY: An unrelated release defect can be silently parked and never diagnosed or re-run by default.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 830-837 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _resume() sets recovered=True before the marker-close PATCH loop succeeds.
  WHY: A failed PATCH can return recovered=True while marker_closed=False, which misleads operators reading the tick log.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:lines 600-604 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The label-create handler swallows GitHub errors beyond the expected already-exists case.
  WHY: A permission or rate-limit failure can result in an unhelpful later issue-creation error and no outage marker or alert.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

(No findings reported.)

  PROBLEM: probe_provider() treats any HTTP 200 response as recovered without inspecting the response body.
  WHY: A provider-side error in a 200 response can close the outage marker and resume reviews while real model calls still fail.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 330-351 (the release-run outage block; specifically the `else` branch at line 342 that calls `provider_outage_record … --only-if-open`) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A failed release run with no provider-outage evidence is still recorded on an open marker and exits before diagnosis.
  WHY: An unrelated release defect is never filed as a heal issue or diagnosed by the intake path.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:latest_review_outcome(), lines 305-328 (specifically the editor-summary branch at lines 326-327: `if _EDITOR_SUMMARY_TEXT in body: latest = {"kind": "summary"}`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: A stale summary can override the current head’s provider_unavailable marker and prevent recovery cleanup.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:record(), lines 600-604 (`try: gh.send("POST", …/labels", …) except GitHubError: pass`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The label-create call swallows every GitHub error, not just an already-exists error.
  WHY: The issue can be posted without its label, or creation can fail with an unhelpful error.

  PROBLEM: Concurrent record() calls can both see an empty marker list and create separate outage markers.
  WHY: One outage can produce duplicate open markers and alerts, and the duplicate-close write can fail.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:record(), lines 595-620 (create / re-list / fallback) and .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml lines 92-94, 111-167 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A queued probe tick can enter recovery after an earlier tick, repeating recovery work and potentially rerunning the same release run.
  WHY: Duplicate recovery actions can increase rerun costs and race with marker comments and close writes.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:_resume(), lines 826-827 (`gh.send("POST", …/issues/{N}/comments", …)`) and 835-836 (the marker PATCH loop) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: _resume() posts the resume comment before the marker PATCH succeeds.
  WHY: A failed PATCH can leave a durable resume comment that causes a retry to treat a release rerun as handled even when the rerun did not happen.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:_resume(), lines 819-820 (`keep_open = bool(summary["errors"]) and attempt < MAX_RESUME_ATTEMPTS`) and the alert_text on line 838 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A final resume attempt with errors can close the marker while the recovery alert obscures the failed work.
  WHY: Operators may not see which consumer repo or release rerun failed without following the marker link.

  PROBLEM: The provider_unavailable reason is defined in multiple locations, allowing the shared marker contract to drift.
